title: When the Alibi Burns
premise: Paloma Montrose, a retired detective turned failing bookshop owner, has quietly solved three deaths the police dismissed as accidents — and kept the files hidden in her cellar. When twin letters arrive, one confessing to a fourth death and one promising a fifth, she realizes the writer knows not only the town's secrets but the contents of her private case files. With the help of her found family — a teenage shop assistant, a disgraced forensic archivist, and the widow of the first 'accident' — Paloma stages a trap using a fabricated fifth victim. The trap works too well: the killer is her late partner's daughter, who learned the trade from his unsolved cases and wanted Paloma to finally pay for burying the truth. In the end, Paloma must choose between turning her in and letting justice outside the law claim one more life; she chooses truth over loyalty, handing everything — including her own three quiet cases — to the police.
about_author: Mirabel Fairweather is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering coroner's inquests before turning to fiction. They live above a secondhand bookshop, which they insist is purely for research.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unsold Books
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet her failing bookshop, her meticulous habits, and the locked cellar where three solved-but-unreported cases sleep in manila folders. A routine day curdles when she notices someone has been reading over her shoulder at night. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Twin Envelopes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Two letters arrive in identical handwriting: one confesses to drowning local handyman Ezra Cole, the other promises 'the next one will be louder.' The police called Ezra's death an accident — a case Paloma closed privately years ago. Beat: cold dread wrapped in flattery; the killer knows her secret.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Reads the Ends First
chapters.summary: Juniper, the seventeen-year-old shop assistant, POV. She notices Paloma's changed behavior and the missing cellar key. Juniper's own loyalty to Paloma — her de facto guardian — is established. Beat: found family warmth undercut by the first lie between them.

chapters.title: What the File Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She reopens the Ezra Cole file and finds a page photographed and returned slightly out of order — proof the killer handled it. She visits the widow, Ruthie Cole, who reveals Ezra received threatening letters too. Beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: An Archivist Out of Favor
chapters.summary: Dev Anand, disgraced forensic archivist, POV. He once lost his career over a discrepancy in a case Paloma worked; now she asks him to authenticate the letters' paper and ink. He agrees, half for redemption, half because he never believed her retirement story. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Pattern
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Analysis shows all three of Paloma's quiet cases share a staged detail — a moved object that only someone with access to original police files would know to replicate. The killer isn't guessing; they've read the evidence rooms. Beat: the hunt becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A letter addressed to Juniper herself arrives: 'Ask her about Harrow Lane.' Juniper confronts Paloma, who admits only fragments of her past. Their fragile family cracks. Beat: betrayal as the price of protection.

chapters.title: Harrow Lane
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Flashback woven through present: twenty-two years ago, Paloma and her partner Declan Quinn botched a stakeout on Harrow Lane; a witness died, the file was buried, and Declan took early retirement and silence. Beat: the alibi she built for him begins to burn.

chapters.title: A Fifth Victim Who Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Paloma and Dev conspire to fabricate a fifth victim — complete fake case file, planted evidence, leaked through a sympathetic records clerk — to bait the killer into revealing how deeply they can see. Beat: dangerous hope; the hunters become authors.

chapters.title: Ruthie Keeps Vigil
chapters.summary: Ruthie Cole's POV. Grieving and furious, she insists on joining the trap, arguing the dead deserve more than Paloma's discretion. Her raw grief forces Paloma to articulate why she never went to the police. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made explicit between two women.

chapters.title: The Bait Is Taken
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Someone accesses the fabricated file within hours of its planting — from inside the records office. Dev traces the login to a credential belonging to a retired officer: Declan Quinn. Beat: vertigo; the past reaches forward.

chapters.title: Declan's Daughter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She learns Declan died two years ago and left everything to his daughter, Maren — who trained as a forensic technician under Dev before he was disgraced. Maren has been invisible in plain sight, volunteering at the records annex. Beat: recognition and horror.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Annex
chapters.summary: Paloma confronts Maren, who neither denies nor flees. Instead she hands Paloma a copy of the Harrow Lane file and says: 'You taught my father that some truths are better buried. I'm just better at it.' Beat: the mirror held up; the killer claims inheritance, not madness.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (unreliable, intimate). Her motive unfolds: she believes the Harrow Lane witness's death was no accident but Paloma's cover-up, and each of her four murders mirrors a case Paloma quietly solved — a syllabus meant to make Paloma confess publicly. Beat: chilling moral symmetry.

chapters.title: Juniper Disobeys
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Ignoring orders, she tails Maren and discovers the 'louder' fifth murder is planned for the anniversary of Harrow Lane — three days away — with Ruthie as the intended victim. Beat: courage outrunning wisdom; stakes become visceral.

chapters.title: The Police, Finally
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cornered by conscience, she brings everything — her three cases, the letters, Harrow Lane — to Detective Inspector Okafor, sacrificing her freedom and reputation. Okafor gives her forty-eight hours of unofficial cooperation. Beat: truth chosen over loyalty, at cost.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The improvised team races to decode Maren's staging pattern; Dev realizes the fifth scene will replicate the Harrow Lane file itself — meaning it must happen where the original events unfolded. Beat: exhaustion, tenderness among the found family, ticking clock.

chapters.title: What Paloma Buried
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, full flashback. The truth of Harrow Lane: the witness's death was genuinely accidental, but Paloma falsified the report to protect Declan from negligence charges — creating the false guilt Maren inherited. Beat: devastating self-knowledge; her alibi burns completely.

chapters.title: Night on Harrow Lane
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs intercut. The team sets the stage at the lane while Maren, anticipating them, moves up her timeline. Juniper is taken when she refuses to leave Ruthie's side. Beat: dread cresting; every plan meets chaos.

chapters.title: The Confession She Demanded
chapters.summary: Climax, Paloma's POV. Maren holds Juniper at the site and demands Paloma confess on camera to murdering the witness. Paloma instead tells the whole truth — including that the death was an accident and Declan knew it — dismantling Maren's entire justification. Maren falters; Okafor's team closes in. Beat: truth as weapon and mercy.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Aftermath: Maren surrenders upon hearing her father's own recorded voice in Dev's recovered archive admitting the accident. Ruthie begins a wrongful-death suit that reopens all the old cases. The bookshop fills with people instead of customers. Beat: grief settling into something like peace.

chapters.title: Everything on the Record
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, closing. She testifies, accepts censure for the buried file, and keeps the bookshop — now with Juniper as partner and Dev repairing the archive he once guarded too well. A final letter arrives, unsigned: 'Thank you for telling the truth. It was louder than any of us.' Beat: justice outside the law ends; justice inside it begins.
